title: Quantum Mechanics Fundamentals
text: Quantum mechanics is the fundamental theory in physics that describes the behavior of nature at the scale of atoms and subatomic particles. Unlike classical mechanics, quantum mechanics involves inherent probabilistic outcomes, described by wave functions that encode the probability of finding a particle in a given state. Key principles include wave-particle duality, the uncertainty principle, and quantum superposition. The theory was developed in the early 20th century by physicists including Niels Bohr, Werner Heisenberg, Erwin Schrödinger, and Max Planck.
